name: Dependant's Pass and Long-Term Visit Pass (family)

value.note: sponsor's fixed monthly salary — genuinely higher than the base S Pass qualifying salary, meaning many S Pass holders cannot sponsor family even though they qualify for the pass itself

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsoring work-pass holder to earn a fixed monthly salary of at least S$6,000.
requirements.fix_path: The sponsor must increase salary to the required threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: This covers legally married spouses and unmarried children under 21 (including legally adopted children).
This covers parents of eligible work-pass holders, at the sponsoring authority's discretion — no fixed statutory salary threshold is published for this specific category, unlike the Dependant's Pass.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate or birth certificate proving family tie
Sponsor's salary evidence meeting the applicable threshold

outcome.duration_length: tracks the sponsor's work pass duration

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL FEATURE confirmed and cross-referenced with sg_s_pass: the Dependant's Pass sponsor salary threshold (S$6,000/month) sits meaningfully ABOVE the S Pass's own base qualifying salary (S$3,300/month) — meaning a large share of S Pass holders qualify for their own work pass but cannot bring family, a real and consequential gap worth surfacing prominently in any 'can I bring my family' comparison view, and genuinely different from most other countries' family-sponsorship routes in this dataset where the family-sponsorship threshold is usually the SAME as (or only modestly above) the base work-permission salary. work_rights marked 'restricted' rather than 'full' since Dependant's Pass holders need a separate Letter of Consent (LOC) or their own work pass to work — not automatic, though the LOC process is described elsewhere as comparatively lightweight once the Dependant's Pass itself is held; not modeled as a full 'full' work-rights entry to avoid overstating the automaticity. Long-Term Visit Pass for parents is explicitly discretionary with no published salary formula — another instance of Singapore's broader pattern (see sg_permanent_residence, sg_naturalisation) of declining to publish fixed criteria for family-adjacent discretionary decisions.
